To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the spin and the weak iso-singlet or -doublet character of the new particles can be determined at the LHC with a high accuracy for most of the parameter space, b) the spin and weak iso-triplet character of the new charged particles can be determined only for a subset of the parameter space and c) the couplings of new particles to the Standard Model particles can be measured for most of the spin and iso-singlet/doublet parameter space.

1) the LHC can measure the mass, spin and couplings of new particles in the two-lepton plus missing energy signature, 2) the couplings of new heavy particles to standard model particles can be measured independently of the spin of the new particle, 3) the spin of the heavy particle can be measured independently from the mass and couplings, and 4) the LHC is able to distinguish the spin of the two heavy particles.

a) the LHC will not only be able to measure the masses of the new particles but also their spin and couplings, and b) the LHC is sensitive to a broad range of new physics models that can be distinguished from each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the general analysis of a class of processes at the LHC, with a focus on the spin and the coupling of the new particles.
the analysis of the most generic signal of two leptonic final states and missing energy.
the general analysis of a signal with two leptons plus missing energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a signal of two leptonic decay products and missing energy at LHC is a smoking gun for new physics, but that a conclusive statement about the properties of the new particles is difficult to obtain.
, with the exception of the cases mentioned, all models of new physics with the signature of two leptons, missing energy and a pair of heavy charged particles can be distinguished at the LHC.
the LHC is able to determine the spin and couplings of new particles in the considered signal class.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for all possible new particle combinations, one can distinguish the new physics models with a significance larger than $ \mathcal{O}(5 \sigma) $.

the LHC will have the capability to determine the spin and couplings of new charged particles with mass up to 1.5 TeV in the case of weak iso-singles, up to 0.9 TeV for iso-doublets, and up to 0. 7 TeV in the iso-triplet case.
, for the LHC, the new particles can be distinguished from each other and from the Standard Model background by their kinematics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LHC is able to distinguish between a large number of models with a two-lepton and missing energy signature.
a large number of possible models can be distinguished by their signatures at the LHC, even when the masses of the new particles cannot be resolved.

, despite the lack of kinematical handles in the two lepton and missing energy signature, a large number of models can be distinguished from the SM at the LHC, and that the LHC will be able to measure the spins and couplings of new particles in many cases.
